en: I am not the body, nor the senses; I am not the internal ego, nor the group of vital breaths, nor the intellect;
I am far removed from wife, children, fields, wealth, and the like.
I am Śiva, the eternal witness, the inner self. || 1 ||
Just as a snake appears in a rope due to ignorance of the rope, so the state of being a living soul (jīva) arises for the Self due to ignorance of its own nature;
through the words of a trustworthy person, that delusion of a snake is destroyed, and it is seen as a rope.
By the words of the Teacher, I am not the individual soul (jīva); I am Śiva. || 2 ||
This entire universe appears within the Self—
which is of the nature of truth, knowledge, and bliss— due to delusion;
like a dream arising from the delusion of sleep, it is not real.
I am pure, complete, eternal, one, and auspicious. || 3 ||
I am not born, nor have I grown, nor have I perished; all the qualities of the material body have been described as such.
Agency and the like do not belong to me, who am composed of consciousness.
For indeed, my very self, which is the agent, is "I am Śiva. || 4 ||
Apart from me, there is nothing else here; the entire universe is a real external object fashioned by illusion,
like the reflection appearing within a mirror.
Therefore, since non-duality shines within me, I am Śiva.
Thus [ends] the work of the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavat, disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavat-pūjyapāda, the illustrious wandering ascetic teacher (paramahaṃsa-parivrājaka-ācārya).
